canonical_frame: Boolean words are 0 or 1; all reserved words are zero; metadata_bits <= 7.
Only listed phases and kind/phase combinations are accepted. Hunk index is below count for active kinds; end kind requires index=count and phase=0.
No-move is mandatory for Add/Delete/end. Old-present is zero before the initial read/derive result is consumed.
The destination index is u64::MAX except phases25/26/31, where it is below delta_length.
Metadata bits must be zero outside successful metadata callbacks. Parent-present is used only at phases5/27 with success.
All non-probe frames are exactly176 bytes with all four payload span words zero.

Phases13/31 append expected bytes at offset176 and then observed bytes immediately after. The exact source length closes both spans; failed reads require an empty observed span. These are opaque bytes; UTF-8 validity is not part of byte equality.
Continuation validation is structural; it is not an authentication of prior host observations. Only the private adapter supplies real host callback results.
semantic_invariants: Exactness is sticky false. Delta metadata/read operations are still selected when it is already false.
Add and move destination perform one initial write, and only NotFound selects optional recursive parent creation plus exactly one retry. In-place updates do not retry.
A move commits destination Add before source metadata/removal. A later failure retains that committed entry; successful removal replaces that same entry.
Failed removal with known old text always selects a reread, including when exactness is already false. HIA compares the returned bytes and preserves the original removal error.
Directory-check errors do not perform the removal-error reread.
Host operations retain the original ExecutorFileSystem, PathUri, sandbox reference and follow_symlinks on every call. Remove is recursive=false/force=false; parent creation is recursive=true.
Summary grouping and public stdout/stderr behavior remain in the unchanged outer caller.
A private adapter transport/framing/materialization error conservatively marks the known committed delta prefix inexact; it does not alter the treatment of ordinary filesystem errors.
